39.intent: TWIST two-over aggregate: the same six names re-dealt, over 1 T20 (SR/Economy x1.5), over 2 Test (Runs/Avg x1.5, SR x0.5), and the ranks flip. Aha: bank the margin in T20, where Aandray Russell's SR 162.41 beats all six; in Test he is a blank (Runs 2), the card to concede Mathew Haydenn's Runs 8625 with, and Dayl Stayn's Test Wickets 439 is your big sure ball. 3 stars: win by 8+ and 7+ balls - Hardik Pandey's Test SR 73.88 beats all six for only 1-2 runs, but it is a sure ball.
39.coach: Same six names, two formats: check which over your hand is strong in before you spend a big number.

40.intent: BOSS two-over aggregate with captains: over 1 ODI (Avg/Wickets x1.5), over 2 Test (Runs/Avg x1.5), one captain for the duel (+15% on its signature stat). The ODI over is theirs (Kumaar Sangakkaara's Runs 14234 beat all six), the Test over yours. Aha: don't captain an ace that wins anyway (Mutti-ah Muraali-tharan's Wickets 800 beat all six); captain Joffra Archer: his ODI Economy 5.21 becomes 4.43 and goes from beating one card to all six. 3 stars: win by 8+ with no wickets lost - Aggressive only on sure balls.
40.coach: Your captain's +15% lifts one stat only. Find the card it turns from a loser into a winner.

42.intent: PRACTISE fog with a wicket race: all out at 2 wickets for either side, and the gambling Circus swipe Aggressive on any above-median number - honest, so loud means strong. Aha: a loud fogged call is also your chance: beat it and you score the band +2 and take a wicket. A loud Wickets call may be Lasithh Malingha's 107, yet Shadaab Khan's Wickets 112 top all six - keep him to answer it, and give quiet calls your cheapest card. 3 stars: win by 8+ and win 4+ balls without losing an Aggressive call.
42.coach: Their swipes are honest, and two wickets is all out. Which card of yours still beats a LOUD number?

43.intent: TEACH Wildcard on a plain T20 over: once per over, swap ONE stat between the card you play and a card in hand - it moves, never copies. Aha: Mitchel Starc's Wickets 79 and Economy 7.74 both beat all six, but he plays once. Swap his 79 onto Ibrahiim Zadran (Wickets 0) and call it: Ibrahiim wins, and Starc keeps Economy 7.74 for a second sure ball. 3 stars: win by 8+ with 2 boundaries - Wickets 79 against a non-bowler (Veerender Sehwaag, Littoon Das, MS Dhonni) is a six.
43.coach: WILDCARD moves one number between the card you play and one in hand. A great number can win twice.

44.intent: BREATHER Wildcard after the L43 teach: you call first, one Wildcard, plain T20. Aha: Brendan MacCalum's Runs 2140 and Mohammaad Nabi's Runs 2300 both beat all six, so open with them; the Wildcard can lend Nabi's 2300 to Matheesha Pathirane (Runs 6) so a spare card wins too while Nabi keeps Wickets 99. Concede Timm Southee's Wickets 164, which beats all six of yours, with your cheapest card. 3 stars: win by 8+ with 2 boundaries - big Runs calls clear the rope once Fakhar Zamaan (1866) and MS Dhonni (1617) are spent.
44.coach: You call first: lead with a number none of theirs can answer, and keep the Wildcard for a spare card.

45.intent: TEACH Mega Pot: dead heats now STACK (2 runs each, up to 8) and carry. Each side holds ONE bowler - Fazalhaqq Farooqi for you, Naveen Ul Haaq for them - and the other ten never bowl. Aha: Wickets 0 v 0 is a dead heat, so once Naveen is spent a non-bowler's Wickets call can only tie; even Farooqi's 66 v Naveen's 67 is a dead heat. Build the pot on purpose, then cash it with Babbar Azam, whose Runs 4223 beat all six. 3 stars: win by 8+ and collect a pot of 4+.
45.coach: Ties now STACK (2 runs each, up to 8). Once their only bowler is gone, which call can only tie?

47.intent: BREATHER Wildcard with no stances - one decision per ball after the L46 combine. Aha: Veerender Sehwaag's SR 145.38 beats all six, but Brendan MacCalum (136.21) and Martin Guptil (135.70) hold it to 2 runs; once they are spent it is a boundary against any card left. Their own aces, Guptil's Runs 3531 and Kagisoo Rabada's Wickets 71, beat all six of yours - concede them with a spare. 3 stars: win by 6+ with 2 boundaries: save your SR calls for late.
47.coach: No stances today. Before you call your best number, count who is still left to answer it.

48.intent: TEACH the bluff tracker: the Parade BLUFF in the fog - Aggressive on a weak number (bottom 60%), quiet on a strong one - the reverse of L42's honest Circus, and the read L53 relies on. The tracker under their card shows how their loud calls turned out. Aha: the quiet fogged call is the danger (Babbar Azam's Runs 4223, Imaad Waseem's Economy 6.27 beat all six): throw Jamess Anderson (Runs 1) at it. A loud call is a bluff: beat it for +2 and a wicket. 3 stars: win by 6+ and win 4+ balls.
48.coach: New rival type: BLUFFERS - loud can mean weak. Watch the tracker under their card: how did loud calls end?

49.intent: TWIST Wildcard + T20 weights: Strike Rate and Economy pay x1.5. Aha: Traviss Head's SR 158.17 beats all six, and Aggressive doubles the weighted band - 10+ runs against every answer except Harry Brookk's SR 145.08 (6). The Wildcard can lend that SR to a spare card while Head still wins on Average 31.22, which also beats all six. Rashhid Khan's Economy 6.15 beats all six of yours: concede it cheaply. 3 stars: win by 8+ and one 9+ run ball - swipe up on that SR once Brookk is spent.
49.coach: Strike Rate and Economy pay x1.5, and Aggressive doubles it. Which of their cards could cap your best call?
